page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 1890 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, scoring 2112.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and 2701.0 in text processing, both placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 13078.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 26677.0. The Intel Xeon processor includes Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 instruction sets, which facilitate efficient low-level operations. Notably, the server achieves top-tier performance in small-model LLM text generation, reaching 373.31 tokens per second with a 135M model. Memory read-only bandwidth reaches 1241.63 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 120.69 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E32-16ds_v6 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The inclusion of 1890 GB of local storage alongside Premium Storage compatibility adds value for data-intensive operations. This server is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing pipelines, and lightweight machine learning inference tasks.
